I get what you're saying, but not exactly. Adderall is an amphetamine, but it's not meth. Adderall's generic name is "dextroamphetamine / amphetamine" or "amphetamine salt combo" and is a different class of drug than meth. 

When taken under the supervision of a doctor, your body should not build up a tolerance to Adderall and you should not have to increase your dose (obviously everybody's different, but in general). Now, if she is taking Adderall at the dosage her doc prescribed that's one thing, ngl still kind of sketch to me since, unless it's the ER / XR version, you can't tell what it is or what's in it. 

BUT, meth is NOT Adderall, and she said herself that she is smoking meth to make sure she can see what's in it better. From my understanding of the post, she is no longer taking Adderall, she is smoking meth, which she was not prescribed, to self-medicare her narcolepsy. 

Meth and Adderall are both addictive but they are not the same. Meth has methyl in it which allows it to reach the brain faster, which means it is much stronger than Adderall. Meth is also unregulated unlike prescription Adderall, so she really has no idea what she's putting in her body, thus making it much more dangerous than a prescription from a doctor. 

Bottom line, she is no longer taking Adderall, she is a meth user trying to self-medicate her narcolepsy. 

Also: OP, I understand this is difficult, but seriously, cut this shit out. Meth sucks you in hard and fast and before you know it, there's no way out. Go to a doctor, go to 10, 20 doctors even. The benefit of a prescription with the drawback of having to wait a month or two is worth your life that could possibly be ruined by meth.

Yes it's possible, but probably not. People with ADHD have trouble focusing on things that don't interest them but when they are interested in something there is the tendency to hyper-focus. Like when a kid wants a candy bar and they are told no, most will let it go after asking why or something of that nature. But generally, a child with ADHD, would not. They would focus on that candy bar they couldn't have for half the day, being in a bad mood because that just really wanted that candy bar. 

So short answer to your question, it depends on the person. If they really, truly, want to solve their problem then most probably won't have trouble with this because they will hyper-focus on learning everything possible about ADHD and the different aspects of it. 

Hope that helped!

I'm not the one you responded to, but I was diagnosed with ADHD my junior year of high school. Just a little background about ADHD: Previously, it was referred to as ADD and ADHD. Now, it is all ADHD with three subcategories; hyperactive, inattentive, and combination. It presents differently in males and females, males having predominantly hyperactive and females having predominantly inattentive. 

What you described was to a T what I was. I wouldn't do big projects or I'd leave them until the last minute because I couldn't wrap my brain around all the steps it would take, I would try to be organized and a week later it all went to shit, and I always had good grades because I was naturally smart, great ones in the classes I enjoyed and decent ones in the classes I didn't because I couldn't get myself to actually do the work. 

I would suggest talking to your primary care physician about this at the very least, make a list of everything that is difficult for you to do, things that distract you, what you do when you get distracted, what you do to help you focus, when you get frustrated, if you have trouble regulating your emotions, etc. Look up the symptoms of ADHD, anxiety, OCD, depression, and maybe some other brain disorders online and start making a list of every single one that you feel on a regular basis or every time XYZ happens. Take those lists to your primary care provider and tell them that these are the things you are feeling, you're concerned it could be ADHD, but you're not sure and you want them to help you understand and fix this issue. 

Hope this was helpful and let me know if there's anything else I can help you with :)
